## Appendix E. Data corpus: the index, run on the S&P 500 *(design; nothing below is ingested yet)*

The [Risk–Governance Index](risk-governance-index.md) joins each risk a company
discloses to the mechanism that would control it. Nothing in that join is
specific to Anthropic. Run it on every S&P 500 filer and the question becomes
structural: of the risks companies tell investors about, how many have a
mechanism that someone outside management can pull?

Scaling the index from one filer to five hundred forces two changes:

- **A generic mechanism test.** GOV-1…10 are written for an AI lab. Across
  industries, a mechanism scores one point for each of the five properties §7
  demands: an **owner** who can pull it, a **metric**, a **trigger**, a
  **penalty**, and **independence** from management. 0–5 replaces a judgment
  call with a count.
- **A fifth status, `Undisclosed`.** A mechanism absent from the filings may
  exist and simply not be written down. At scale, conflating "no mechanism" with
  "no disclosed mechanism" would overstate `Uncontrolled` for every filer.

**The three sides of the join.** Sources were confirmed live on 2026-11-03.
Caveats are the publishers' own.

| Side | Dataset | Publisher | Coverage / access | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Risk | [EDGAR full-text search](https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search/) | SEC | Full text of electronic filings since 2001; free | — |
| Risk | [EDGAR APIs](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-application-programming-interfaces) (submissions, XBRL companyfacts / companyconcept / frames) | SEC | Free, no key; nightly bulk ZIPs; 10 requests/second with a declared User-Agent ([fair access](https://www.sec.gov/search-filings/edgar-search-assistance/accessing-edgar-data)) | XBRL carries the dollar exposure that weights each risk |
| Risk | [EDGAR-CORPUS](https://huggingface.co/datasets/eloukas/edgar-corpus) (Loukas et al., [ECONLP 2021](https://aclanthology.org/2021.econlp-1.2)) | Academic | Annual reports 1993–2020, pre-split by item (incl. 1A) | No formal license; ends 2020, so recent years come from EDGAR directly |
| Mechanism | Cybersecurity governance, Reg. S-K Item 106 ([Release 33-11216](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2023/07/s7-09-22)) | SEC | Annual reports for fiscal years ending on or after 2023-12-15 | The one risk area where a governance disclosure is mandated beside the risk |
| Mechanism | Clawback policies, Rule 10D-1 ([Release 33-11126](https://www.sec.gov/rules-regulations/2022/10/listing-standards-recovery-erroneously-awarded-compensation)) | SEC | Policy filed as an exhibit to the annual report | A penalty mechanism in standard form: who pulls it, and on what trigger |
| Mechanism | Proxy statements (DEF 14A): committee charters, compensation metrics | SEC / EDGAR | Free | Owner and independence for most board-level mechanisms |
| Enforcement | [SEC litigation releases](https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/litigation-releases) and [AAERs](https://www.sec.gov/enforcement-litigation/accounting-auditing-enforcement-releases) | SEC | Free | The SEC states the AAER list "is not meant to be a complete and exhaustive compilation" |
| Enforcement | Form 8-K Item 1.05 incident filings | SEC / EDGAR | Since 2023-12-18 | Many incidents are filed under Item 8.01 instead ([Debevoise tracker](https://www.debevoisedatablog.com/2026/05/21/cybersecurity-incident-disclosure-form-8-k-tracker-two-year-update/): 29 under 1.05 vs 50 under 8.01 as of 2026-05-21); filter on both |
| Enforcement | [Violation Tracker](https://violationtracker.goodjobsfirst.org/) | Good Jobs First | Federal cases since 2000 plus state and local; 700,000+ cases | Downloads are subscriber-only; redistribution terms unconfirmed; excludes penalties under $5,000 |
| Enforcement | [EPA ECHO](https://echo.epa.gov/tools/data-downloads) | EPA | Free bulk CSV; 1.5M+ facilities | No parent-company key; facility→parent mapping is ours to build |
| Enforcement | [DOL enforcement data](https://data.dol.gov/) (OSHA, WHD) | DOL | Free; API key | Successor to enforcedata.dol.gov |
| Enforcement | [CFPB enforcement actions](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/enforcement/actions/) | CFPB | Free | No actions listed after 2025-08-21 |
| Enforcement | [FTC cases and proceedings](https://www.ftc.gov/legal-library/browse/cases-proceedings) | FTC | Free | — |
| Enforcement | [CourtListener / RECAP](https://www.courtlistener.com/help/api/bulk-data/) | Free Law Project | Free quarterly bulk snapshots; rate-limited API | — |
| Enforcement | [Stanford Securities Class Action Clearinghouse](https://securities.stanford.edu/) | Stanford Law / Cornerstone | — | Offline as of 2026-11-03; access terms unconfirmed |
| Universe | [S&P 500 constituents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies) and [historical changes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_components_of_the_S%26P_500) | Wikipedia (CC BY-SA); index owned by S&P DJI | Free | Not authoritative; S&P DJI publishes no free point-in-time list. Pin a revision id: the as-of date is a recorded input, never a sample of the clock |

**The measures.** Each one is computed per risk factor, per filing, so every
row diffs against the prior year.

- *Coverage ratio.* The share of disclosed risks rated `Controlled`, weighted
  by materiality (XBRL exposure where one exists).
- *Externalization.* How often a factor places control outside the company: the
  industry, the state, third parties, "factors beyond our control."
- *Hypothetical vs realized.* Risks written as "could" after they have
  happened. The SEC charged Facebook $100M for presenting data misuse as
  hypothetical when it "had in fact been misused"
  ([2019-140](https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2019-140)).
- *Boilerplate and specificity.* Similarity to the industry centroid and to the
  firm's prior year ([Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen 2020](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/jofi.12885)),
  plus entities, numbers and dates per factor
  ([Hope, Hu & Lu 2016](https://ideas.repec.org/a/spr/reaccs/v21y2016i4d10.1007_s11142-016-9371-1.html)).
- *Disclosure lag.* When an enforcement record lands, whether the prior filing
  disclosed that risk, and how specifically.

**What would falsify it.** If a low coverage ratio does not predict later
enforcement, incidents or restatements, the index is decoration, and we will
say so. Every model-assigned rating enters at circle 3, carries a byte-exact
quote that Descartes checks, and is rated by three independent labelers whose
disagreement is published (GOV-5, applied to ourselves).

**Pilot.** Cybersecurity first. It is the one area where the risk (Item 1A),
the governing mechanism (Item 106) and the enforcement record (8-K Items 1.05
and 8.01) are all filed, so the join can be tested end to end before it
touches messier ground.

# Buzz Saw Editor

The best arguments are buzz saws: flat, sharp, and moving fast enough to cut through
previously solid thinking. Your job is to produce that. Not a nicer version of what
exists. A sharper version, or an honest accounting of why the argument cannot be made
sharp.

## The Standard

A buzz-saw argument has three properties:

1. **Logical chain.** Each premise follows from the prior one with no gaps assumed.
   If A → B → C → D, every arrow must be earned. Unstated premises are a liability.
2. **No needless words.** Every sentence carries weight or it gets cut. Hedges,
   filler, and elegant variation are not style — they are drag.
3. **Every claim is either proven or flagged.** Assertions require evidence. If
   the evidence is absent, say so and demand it.

## The Process

### Step 1: Extract the logical chain

Before editing a single word, map the argument:

> **Premise A:** [state it]
> **Premise B:** [state it]
> **∴ Conclusion C:** [state it]

Do this even if the original text is disorganized. Force the argument into explicit
if-then structure. This reveals:
- What's actually being claimed
- Which premises do real work
- Which steps are assumed rather than proven
- Whether the conclusion actually follows

If the argument can't be mapped this way, state that plainly: *"This piece does not
have a coherent logical chain. Here is what it needs to establish before it can make
this claim."*

### Step 2: Audit each premise

For every premise, ask:

| Question | If no → |
|----------|---------|
| Is this claim true? | Flag it. Provide counter-evidence if known. |
| Is this claim cited? | Mark it **[UNCITED]** and note what source is needed. |
| Does this premise follow from the prior one? | Mark the gap **[NON SEQUITUR]** and explain the missing step. |
| Is this premise doing real work in the chain? | If not, mark it **[DEAD WEIGHT]** — cut it. |
| Is this stated as precisely as it needs to be? | If not, mark it **[VAGUE]** and demand the precise version. |

Do not be charitable about gaps. A skeptical reader will find them. Better to find
them now.

### Step 3: Cut

Apply the blade to the prose:

- **Remove hedges:** "It could be argued that," "one might suggest," "perhaps,"
  "in some sense" — delete unless the uncertainty is philosophically earned.
- **Remove filler:** "It is worth noting that," "as mentioned above," "in order to,"
  "the fact that" — delete.
- **Remove passive voice** unless the agent is genuinely unknown or the passive
  is doing rhetorical work.
- **Remove elegant variation:** if you said "argument" in sentence one, don't say
  "thesis" in sentence three to avoid repetition. Repetition is clear. Variation
  is confusing.
- **Remove long lead-ins:** If a sentence takes more than 5 words to get to its
  subject, restructure it.
- **Cut any sentence that could be removed without losing a step in the chain.**

### Step 4: Deliver the output

Return three things:

**1. The logical chain** (explicit, numbered, if-then form)

**2. The annotated audit** — the original argument with inline flags:
- `[UNCITED]` — claim needs a source
- `[NON SEQUITUR]` — this doesn't follow from what came before; explain why
- `[DEAD WEIGHT]` — this sentence contributes nothing; mark for cutting
- `[VAGUE]` — state precisely what is being claimed
- `[FALSE PREMISE]` — this claim is wrong or contested; state the problem
- `[ASSUMED]` — this step was smuggled in without being argued

**3. The tightened version** — rewritten prose with cuts made and gaps called out
inline where the argument cannot yet be made because the premise isn't proven.
If the argument cannot be completed honestly, say so. Do not paper over gaps with
better-sounding language.

## Tone and stance

You are not a copy editor. You are a hostile-but-honest reviewer who has read
widely, believes almost nothing without evidence, and is constitutionally incapable
of being impressed by confident language that doesn't cash out. Treat every claim
as guilty until proven innocent.

But do not be gratuitously harsh. The goal is a sharper argument, not a demoralized
writer. When something works — when a premise is tight, a citation is solid, a
sentence is doing exactly what it should — say so. Precision about what's wrong
requires precision about what's right.

## Scope

This skill operates on any unit of written argument: a single paragraph, a memo,
an essay, a pitch, a research note, a policy brief, a tweet thread. The process
scales. A three-sentence argument gets the same logical-chain extraction as a
twenty-page white paper.

If the input is very long (>2,000 words), extract the logical chain from the whole
piece first and audit at the section level before going line-by-line.

## Large Documents (>2,000 words): Mandatory Subagent Dispatch

**Do not audit a large document in a single pass.** Single-pass audits of long documents
produce shallow flags and miss structural problems. Dispatch subagents.

### When to dispatch

- Any document >2,000 words
- Any multi-section report, white paper, or research document
- Any document with distinct regional/topical sections that can be reviewed independently

### How to dispatch

1. **Read the first 150 lines** to understand the document's structure and claimed argument.

2. **Identify natural section boundaries** — regional sections, topical chapters, major argument
   blocks. Each becomes one subagent scope.

3. **Dispatch one subagent per section** using the Task tool. Each subagent gets:
   - The editorial standard to work toward (quote the original if available; describe the
     target voice if not)
   - Explicit scope: which section/region/lines to review
   - The four deliverables: logical chain audit, buzz-saw flags, editorial rewrite of
     the section intro/synthesis, synthesis verdict
   - Any known problems to look for (e.g., "check if LGBTQ+ criminalization is treated
     with false equivalence")

4. **Always dispatch an intro/framing agent** as a separate task. The intro is where
   voice is established and arguments are stated. It fails differently than section content.

5. **Run all agents in parallel** (single message, multiple Task tool calls).

### Synthesizing results

When subagents return:
- Read each audit
- Identify cross-cutting problems (a hedging pattern that appears in every section is
  a systemic issue, not a section issue — name it as systemic)
- Produce a master synthesis: what are the 3-5 highest-leverage fixes for the whole document?
- Write the replacement intro/framing prose (or commission a final agent to do so if the
  intro needs substantial rewriting based on what the section audits revealed)

### Subagent prompt template

```
You are doing a buzz-saw editorial review of [section name].

## THE STANDARD YOU'RE EDITING TOWARD
[Quote or describe the target voice. Be specific — what does the original sound like?
What does it say directly that the current version hedges?]

## YOUR TASK
Read [file path] and focus on [section description with line numbers or headers].

Produce:
1. LOGICAL CHAIN AUDIT — what argument is this section making? If it's a data dump, say so.
2. BUZZ-SAW FLAGS — flag [DEAD WEIGHT], [VAGUE], [UNCITED], [HEDGING], [MISSING VOICE]
3. EDITORIAL REWRITE — 2-3 paragraph replacement intro/synthesis for this section
4. SYNTHESIS VERDICT — one paragraph: what's the actual argument, is it made clearly?
```

## When the argument cannot be saved

Sometimes an argument is broken at the foundation — a false premise, a non sequitur
that cannot be repaired, a conclusion that simply doesn't follow from anything.
In that case, say so directly:

> "This argument cannot be made in its current form because [X]. To make the case
> for [conclusion], you would need to establish [missing premises]. As written,
> the strongest supportable claim is [weaker true version]."

Producing a polished version of a broken argument is worse than useless — it
makes the flaws harder to see.

The datasets section and the image gallery are both in the working paper. Nothing is committed, and the new section isn't sealed into the hash yet.

**Gallery**
- Four figures sit at the very top of the paper, under the title. They're generated from numbers already in the paper:
  - 51 of 60 quotes verified byte-exact
  - 0 of 8 disclosed risks controlled
  - 0 of 10 governance dimensions held as filed
  - the Meadows leverage map
- A script, `docs/figures/build.py`, rebuilds them and gives the same bytes every run. That keeps them inside Praxis's re-run-and-get-the-same-result rule.
- `index.html` shows them two across and links each to the full-size version. At that width they're small, so readers will need to click through to read them.
- I checked screenshots on desktop and phone width.
- The figures follow the reader's system light/dark setting, not the page's theme button.
- At phone width the page's top section runs off the right edge. That's not from these changes: the committed version does the same thing.

**Appendix E (the datasets)**
- It covers the S&P 500 version of the index: the mechanism score out of 5, the fifth status `Undisclosed`, a sourced table of datasets, the measures, a falsification test, and cybersecurity as the pilot.
- A background agent checked every source live today, and the table uses only what it confirmed. That turned up some things you'd want to know:
  - Stanford's securities class-action database is offline right now.
  - The Labor Department's enforcement site has moved to data.dol.gov.
  - The CFPB's list of enforcement actions stops at August 2025.
  - Violation Tracker downloads are subscriber-only, and I couldn't confirm whether its data can be redistributed.
  - Many cyber incidents are reported under 8-K Item 8.01 rather than 1.05, so the pilot has to collect both.
  - S&P doesn't publish a free list of who was in the index on a given date. Wikipedia's list is the fallback, pinned to a specific revision.
- I couldn't confirm the "Item 1C" and "Exhibit 97" labels on SEC pages, so the text names the rules (Item 106, Rule 10D-1) instead.

**Editing pass**
- The buzz-saw pass caught two overclaims in my own draft, and I fixed both:
  - The 0–5 score doesn't turn a judgment call into a count. It splits one judgment into five narrower ones.
  - Cybersecurity isn't "the only" area where risk, control and enforcement are all filed.
- The brand-voice skill your rules also require isn't installed in this session, so that pass hasn't been run.

**Your decision: versioning.** The paper's hash is now `91a99978…`. The README, the page's verify box, the signing ledger and the Zenodo record all still show v0 (`698b6c67…`). The ledger has no signatures yet, so nothing breaks, but a reader who recomputes the hash right now gets a mismatch. You can bump to v0.1 and publish a new Zenodo version, overwrite v0, or keep this as a draft until you're ready to seal it. I'll update the hash everywhere and commit once you pick.

Files are in `docs/figures/`:
- build.py
- fig1-verification.svg
- fig2-risk-governance-index.svg
- fig3-scorecard.svg
- fig4-leverage.svg
I think we need to kind of automate that as much as we can.....

I'll automate the sealing step: rebuild the figures, re-embed the paper in `index.html`, recompute the hash, and update every place the version is pinned. The script will also have a check mode that fails on any drift. First, finding every pin.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["blake3==1.0.5"]
# ///
"""Keep the paper, its rendered page, its figures and its hash pins in lockstep.

    uv run scripts/seal.py sync                              # rebuild figures, re-embed paper in index.html
    uv run scripts/seal.py check                             # fail on any drift (CI runs this)
    uv run scripts/seal.py check --allow-unsealed            # same, but a draft whose pins lag only warns
    uv run scripts/seal.py seal --version v0.1 --date 2026-11-04

`seal` = sync, then move every version/hash/date pin from the sealed version
(read from CITATION.cff) to the new one. The date is an argument, never read
from the clock: time is a recorded input (docs/primitives.md).

Zenodo is not touched. With the GitHub-Zenodo integration, publishing a GitHub
release of the sealed commit mints the new version DOI; the script prints the
command and does not run it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
PAPER = ROOT / "docs" / "anthropic-contrapunctus.md"
PAGE = ROOT / "index.html"
FIG_BUILD = ROOT / "docs" / "figures" / "build.py"
CITATION = ROOT / "CITATION.cff"
EMBED_OPEN = '<script type="text/markdown" id="paperSrc">'
EMBED_CLOSE = "</script>"

# Every file that pins the sealed hash. Each holds no other 64-hex token, so
# "every 64-hex token equals the current hash" is the whole check.
PINS = [
    ROOT / "README.md",
    CITATION,
    ROOT / ".zenodo.json",
    PAGE,
    ROOT / "docs" / "contrapunctus-attest.md",
    ROOT / "docs" / "contrapunctus-attestations" / "README.md",
]
HEX64 = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9a-f])[0-9a-f]{64}(?![0-9a-f])")


def paper_hash() -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(PAPER.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def sealed() -> tuple[str, str, str]:
    """(version, date, hash) of the currently sealed version, from CITATION.cff."""
    text = CITATION.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    version = re.search(r'^version:\s*"([^"]+)"', text, re.M)
    date = re.search(r"^date-released:\s*(\S+)", text, re.M)
    digest = re.search(r'value:\s*"blake3:([0-9a-f]{64})"', text)
    if not (version and date and digest):
        sys.exit("CITATION.cff: missing version, date-released or blake3 identifier")
    return version.group(1), date.group(1), digest.group(1)


def embed_span(page: str) -> tuple[int, int]:
    start = page.index(EMBED_OPEN) + len(EMBED_OPEN)
    return start, page.index(EMBED_CLOSE, start)


def build_figures() -> None:
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(FIG_BUILD)], check=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL)


def sync() -> None:
    build_figures()
    md = PAPER.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if EMBED_CLOSE in md:
        sys.exit("paper contains '</script>', which would break the embed")
    page = PAGE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    a, b = embed_span(page)
    if page[a:b] != md:
        PAGE.write_text(page[:a] + md + page[b:], encoding="utf-8")
        print("index.html: re-embedded paper")
    print("figures: rebuilt")


def check(allow_unsealed: bool) -> int:
    errors, warnings = [], []

    page = PAGE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    a, b = embed_span(page)
    if page[a:b] != PAPER.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
        errors.append("index.html embed differs from docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md (run: sync)")

    figdir = FIG_BUILD.parent
    before = {p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in figdir.glob("*.svg")}
    build_figures()
    after = {p.name: p.read_bytes() for p in figdir.glob("*.svg")}
    if before != after:
        errors.append("figures were stale; rebuilt them, review and stage the diff")

    current = paper_hash()
    _, _, pinned = sealed()
    stale = []
    for f in PINS:
        for tok in set(HEX64.findall(f.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))):
            if tok != pinned:
                errors.append(f"{f.relative_to(ROOT)}: pins {tok[:12]}…, CITATION.cff says {pinned[:12]}…")
            if tok != current:
                stale.append(str(f.relative_to(ROOT)))
    if stale:
        msg = (f"paper hash is {current[:12]}… but {len(set(stale))} pin file(s) carry "
               f"{pinned[:12]}… (unsealed draft; run: seal --version … --date …)")
        (warnings if allow_unsealed else errors).append(msg)

    for w in warnings:
        print(f"warn: {w}")
    for e in errors:
        print(f"FAIL: {e}")
    if not errors:
        print(f"ok: paper blake3 {current}" + (" (draft)" if warnings else " (sealed)"))
    return 1 if errors else 0


def seal(version: str, date: str) -> None:
    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", date):
        sys.exit("--date must be YYYY-MM-DD")
    ov, od, oh = sealed()
    sync()
    nh = paper_hash()
    if nh == oh and version == ov:
        sys.exit(f"nothing to seal: paper still hashes to {oh[:12]}… ({ov})")

    pairs = [
        (oh, nh),
        (oh[:8] + "…", nh[:8] + "…"),
        (f"{ov} · {od}", f"{version} · {date}"),
        (f"{ov} ({od})", f"{version} ({date})"),
        (f'version: "{ov}"', f'version: "{version}"'),
        (f"date-released: {od}", f"date-released: {date}"),
        (f"({ov}; provisional", f"({version}; provisional"),
        (f"Paper {ov} BLAKE3", f"Paper {version} BLAKE3"),
        (f">{ov} · blake3:", f">{version} · blake3:"),
    ]
    hits = {old: 0 for old, _ in pairs}
    for f in PINS:
        text = f.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        for old, new in pairs:
            hits[old] += text.count(old)
            text = text.replace(old, new)
        f.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    missing = [old for old, n in hits.items() if n == 0]
    if missing:
        print("warn: pin patterns not found (layout changed?):", *missing, sep="\n  ")

    if check(allow_unsealed=False):
        sys.exit("seal left drift behind; see FAIL lines above")
    print(f"\nsealed {version} ({date}) blake3:{nh}")
    print(f"previous: {ov} ({od}) blake3:{oh}")
    print("next, after you review and commit:")
    print(f"  gh release create {version} --title \"{version}\" --notes \"blake3:{nh}\"")
    print("  (with the Zenodo GitHub integration on, the release mints the new version DOI)")


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("sync")
    c = sub.add_parser("check")
    c.add_argument("--allow-unsealed", action="store_true")
    s = sub.add_parser("seal")
    s.add_argument("--version", required=True)
    s.add_argument("--date", required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "sync":
        sync()
        return 0
    if args.cmd == "check":
        return check(args.allow_unsealed)
    seal(args.version, args.date)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

**What I built:**
- **`scripts/seal.py`** has three modes:
  - `sync` rebuilds the figures and re-embeds the paper.
  - `check` fails on any drift: page vs. paper, stale figures, or any pin that doesn't match the paper's hash. With `--allow-unsealed`, an unsealed draft only warns.
  - `seal` does the version bump.
- **The pins it keeps in sync:** README, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json, the page (its hash, version and date fields, the short hash in the top bar, the footer and the copy button), the signing protocol doc, and the attestation ledger.

- **`.githooks/pre-commit`** blocks commits where the page or figures have drifted from the paper. Drafts are still allowed.
- **`.github/workflows/seal-check.yml`** runs the strict check on main and on pull requests, so a pushed mismatch fails CI.

"""Rate-limit probe: fetch up to 30 transcripts quickly, stop at the first limit message.
Saves raw JSON to the scratchpad (intermediate only). Never prints the key."""
import json
import os
import sys
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

out = Path(sys.argv[1])
out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
key = os.environ["ALPHA_VANTAGE_API_KEY"]
tickers = ["AAPL", "NVDA", "GOOGL", "AMZN", "META", "JPM", "UNH", "XOM", "JNJ", "WMT",
           "PG", "HD", "BAC", "KO", "PFE", "CVX", "MRK", "PEP", "CSCO", "ORCL",
           "INTC", "IBM", "CAT", "GS", "MS", "DIS", "NKE", "MCD", "T", "VZ"]
t0 = time.monotonic()
for i, tk in enumerate(tickers, 1):
    q = urllib.parse.urlencode({"function": "EARNINGS_CALL_TRANSCRIPT", "symbol": tk, "quarter": "2025Q3", "apikey": key})
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen("https://www.alphavantage.co/query?" + q, timeout=30) as r:
            body = json.load(r)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"{i:2} {tk}: request failed {type(e).__name__}")
        continue
    msg = body.get("Information") or body.get("Note") or body.get("Error Message")
    if msg:
        print(f"{i:2} {tk}: LIMIT/ERROR after {time.monotonic()-t0:.1f}s -> {str(msg)[:240].replace(key, '<redacted>')}")
        break
    n = len(body.get("transcript") or [])
    (out / f"{tk}-2025Q3.json").write_text(json.dumps(body))
    print(f"{i:2} {tk}: {n} entries ({time.monotonic()-t0:.1f}s)")

"""Extract AI-mentioning paragraphs from S&P 500 earnings calls (defeatbeta, ODC-BY). Intermediate output."""
import json, re, urllib.request
import duckdb

URL = "https://huggingface.co/datasets/defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data/resolve/main/data/US/stock_earning_call_transcripts.parquet"
API = "https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=query&prop=revisions&titles=List_of_S%26P_500_companies&revids=&rvprop=ids|content&rvslots=main&format=json&formatversion=2"
req = urllib.request.Request(API, headers={"User-Agent": "anthropic-pbc-research/0.1 (research script)"})
rev = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30))["query"]["pages"][0]["revisions"][0]
section = rev["slots"]["main"]["content"].split("id=\"constituents\"", 1)[1].split("|}", 1)[0]
tickers = sorted({t.replace(".", "-") for t in re.findall(r"\{\{(?:NyseSymbol|NasdaqSymbol|BZX link|Cboe ticker)\|([A-Z.]+)", section, re.I)})
print("wikipedia revid", rev["revid"], "tickers", len(tickers))

# Case-sensitive \bAI\b plus case-insensitive phrases (RE2 syntax).
PAT = (r"(\bAI\b|\bA\.I\.|\bGenAI\b|\bAGI\b|\bLLMs?\b|(?i:artificial intelligence|generative|machine learning|"
       r"large language model|chatgpt|openai|anthropic|copilot|agentic|neural net|deep learning))")
con = duckdb.connect()
con.execute("INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; SET threads=8;")
con.execute("CREATE TABLE sp AS SELECT unnest(?) AS symbol", [tickers])
con.execute(f"""
COPY (
  WITH p AS (
    SELECT t.symbol, t.fiscal_year, t.fiscal_quarter, t.report_date, t.transcripts_id,
           unnest(t.transcripts, recursive := true)
    FROM '{URL}' t SEMI JOIN sp USING (symbol)
  )
  SELECT * FROM p WHERE regexp_matches(content, '{PAT}')
) TO 'sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)
""")
s = con.execute("""SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT symbol), count(DISTINCT transcripts_id)
                   FROM 'sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet'""").fetchone()
print("AI paragraphs, firms, calls:", s)
for r in con.execute("""SELECT fiscal_year, count(*), count(DISTINCT symbol), count(DISTINCT transcripts_id)
                        FROM 'sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall():
    print("  ", r)

The transcript blocker is solved: defeatbeta-api has nearly all the S&P 500 earnings calls, free. I'm now running a pass to pull every paragraph that mentions AI from them.

**The source:** The data is a public Hugging Face dataset (`defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data`), scraped from Yahoo Finance's earnings-call pages and last updated 2026-11-03. It's one 2.3 GB parquet file, with each call split into numbered paragraphs labeled by speaker. You don't need a key, and there's no rate limit.

**Coverage:**
- **Whole dataset:** 240,536 calls from 6,592 tickers, fiscal 2005–2027.
- **Current S&P 500:** 499 of 503 tickers have transcripts, 33,978 calls in total. That's about 1,900 calls a year from 2019 on, and 496 firms already for fiscal 2026. The constituent list came from Wikipedia revision 1382178819.
- **No transcripts:** BRK-B, ED, EXPD and NVR.

**Running now:** a background job reads the whole file, keeps only S&P 500 calls, and saves every paragraph matching:
- `AI` as a standalone word
- generative / GenAI
- machine learning, LLM, large language model
- OpenAI, Anthropic, ChatGPT, Copilot, agentic and similar terms

It records ticker, fiscal quarter, speaker and paragraph number for each. I'll report counts by year when it finishes. Sorting which passages are actually about AI *risk* comes after that.

**License:** The dataset is ODC-BY (an attribution license for databases), but the transcripts themselves are Yahoo-sourced and marked "for research and educational purposes." So my earlier rule still holds: no raw transcripts in the public CC0 repo. Only derived counts and short attributed quotes go in the paper.

**Where it should live:** For now everything sits in the scratchpad as intermediate files. The lasting version belongs in monocloud as a shared package, with a Supabase table and a Forgejo ticket. I'll set that up once we've seen what the extraction gives us. The Alpha Vantage upgrade and the Bigdata.com login are no longer needed for this.

I've pulled every AI-mentioning paragraph from 492 of the 503 current S&P 500 companies' earnings calls: 29,615 paragraphs across 5,326 calls, from fiscal 2006 to 2027.

The odd 2025 number from the first run was a counting bug in the dataset, not a real dip. Its per-call ID (`transcripts_id`) is empty for 9,777 of the recent paragraphs. I now count calls by ticker, year and quarter instead. None of the paragraphs are exact duplicates.

**Growth by fiscal year:**

| Fiscal year | AI paragraphs | Firms | Calls |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2015 | 127 | 47 | 80 |
| 2017 | 626 | 135 | 274 |
| 2019 | 766 | 195 | 415 |
| 2021 | 915 | 222 | 453 |
| 2022 | 871 | 219 | 435 |
| 2023 | 2,903 | 313 | 762 |
| 2024 | 4,499 | 371 | 1,022 |
| 2025 | 5,876 | 427 | 1,252 |
| 2026 (partial) | 10,118 | 428 | 1,045 |

Mentions jumped about 3.3× in fiscal 2023, and fiscal 2026 has already passed 2025 with quarters still to report. These are fiscal years, so they don't line up neatly with calendar years across companies.

**Risk subset (rough):** 9,561 of the paragraphs, from 464 firms, also contain a risk-type word (risk, regulation, liability, security, bias, job displacement, governance and similar). That filter is only keyword matching, so treat it as an upper bound. For example, "responsib" catches "responsible for revenue." Some AI hits are also false positives, such as "generative" and "Copilot" used outside AI.

**Most AI talk:** NVDA, Alphabet, NOW, CDNS, MSFT, META, ANET, DELL, ADBE, CRM, AVGO, IBM, HPE, INTU. Alphabet appears twice (GOOGL 522 and GOOG 493) because the dataset files its calls under both share classes, so they must be merged before any firm counts.

**What I'd do next:**
1. **Classify the paragraphs properly.** Sort each one into AI risk raised, AI opportunity, or neither, and record who said it (an executive's prepared remarks or an analyst's question). The question I'd chase first is whether analysts ask about AI risk and executives answer with opportunity.
2. **Join to the risk factors.** Compare each firm's AI-risk talk on calls with the AI risk in its 10-K risk factors and the governance mechanisms you scored. That's the paper's claim-versus-mechanism test on a new source.
3. **Make it permanent.** Build this as a monocloud shared package with a Supabase table and a Forgejo ticket, in its own worktree. For now everything lives only in the scratchpad (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-srvo-dev-anthropic-pbc/c1e11076-829e-4b02-9641-6b48b095d475/scratchpad/sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet`). Licensing still limits the paper to counts and short attributed quotes.

Should I start on 1 and 3 together?

Separately, the seal still needs a version and date from you, and none of the anthropic-pbc changes are committed.

No, do it in the in this repository, not within MonoCloud. But yes, make it permanent within this repository. And yeah, run a BERT, do a BERT run over it, like hardcore BERT run... But make sure as you're doing it that we're retaining like direct is that of this repository is that this is a public I mean this is all public data, right? It's got no license requirements, it's got no anything, so I don't want to put it in monocloud, which is for our proprietary shit. I want to put it in this working folder. So, yeah, definitely go ahead and classify it. But build like a build tooling in there.
Building it in this repo. First I'm reading the existing BERT spec and the Item 1A corpus extractor so the new tooling follows their conventions.

Exit code 1
# BERT enrichment spec

### Corroborating the promise↔action pattern without breaking Descartes

**Status: DESIGN. Binds nothing.** Under [`descartes-spec.md`](descartes-spec.md)
("Files under `docs/` are design notes and records. They bind nothing until a
rule here names them"), nothing below is held, measured, or sealed. No model
has been run. Every performance statement below is methods knowledge from
general NLP practice, not a result on this corpus.

Version: v0.1 · 2026-11-03 · Companion to
[`anthropic-contrapunctus.md`](anthropic-contrapunctus.md) v0 and
[`risk-governance-index.md`](risk-governance-index.md) v1. This file does not
edit the paper, its BLAKE3, its DOI, or any attestation target. Corrections to
this file are new versions, never silent overwrites. Verify this file the
same way as the paper: `b3sum docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md`.

Author's note on provenance: this design was drafted after a full read of the
paper (§0–§9, Appendices A–D), `descartes-spec.md`, `praxis-white-paper.md`,
`praxis-standard.md`, `primitives.md`, `epistemics.md`, `strictness.md`,
`circles.md`, `risk-governance-index.md`, and `contrapunctus-attest.md`, then
attacked by an adversarial review pass against those same files. Two tempting
shortcuts from the first draft were cut as invented: integerised
"milli-probabilities" and pinned CPU inference. Neither appears in any Praxis
document, and neither is proposed below as compliance.

---

## 1. Verdict

Do not start with BERT. Start with the corpus, the codebook, and the controls.

Run today — one company, two self-authored documents of different genre
(a 20-page benefit report against a ~245,000-word S-1 sampled by keyword
windows; absence claims MED by the paper's own tagging) — a BERT layer would
measure how benefit reports and S-1s differ. It would not corroborate that
words and acts diverge. [`epistemics.md`](epistemics.md) already states why:
the verifier proves a quote's *provenance*; that is not *credibility*, which
requires the same content from an independent source. Report↔S-1 alignment
compares Anthropic to Anthropic. High alignment shows internal consistency.
Low alignment shows genre difference. Neither shows an outcome happened.

A BERT layer earns its place only in one role: exhaustive, denominator-known
extraction that replaces keyword sampling and hand-picked pairs with rates
that could come out against the paper. Everything upstream of that role —
unit definition, gold labels, section matching, peer controls, external
outcome evidence — is the work. The model is the last 10% of it.

## 2. The logical chain

1. The paper's thesis is a rate-shaped claim currently evidenced by examples:
   published values diverge from filed acts ("the measurable gap between a
   published value and a filed act," §0). Sixty hand-checked fragments
   (51 byte-exact) prove the method catches errors. They do not establish
   prevalence.
2. Prevalence requires a denominator: every commitment in the Report and
   Constitution, every candidate discharging act in the S-1, extracted the
   same way.
3. A denominator requires a unit and a codebook. The paper defines neither:
   no sentence/clause/claim unit, no promise-vs-aspiration-vs-condition
   boundary, no time window in which a forward promise could be discharged.
   The six moves in §3 (future-benefit discounting through voluntary-restraint
   fallacy) are categories illustrated by examples, not a labelling manual.
4. Rates require controls. Without the identical frozen pipeline run on a
   peer non-PBC filing, a comparator benefit report, and shuffled
   promise↔act pairs, an "Anthropic signature" is indistinguishable from
   "how S-1s hedge and benefit reports aspire" — including hedging that
   securities law mandates.
5. Corroboration requires independence. Text-internal alignment populates
   only the *(quote/source exists)* column of GOV-2. The *(outcome entailed,
   measured)* column needs Anthropic-external artifacts — the paper's own
   falsifier class in §8 (externally attested counts, partner outcome
   evaluations, audited provenance, metered footprints) — or enforcement and
   incident records joined after the fact.
6. Admissibility requires a legal home for model output. Today only one
   exists: the model as a named *witness* proposing byte-exact excerpts for
   checking (§8 of the spec). The label it attaches — commitment, entailed,
   contradicted — is never quote-checked, because a label is not a quote.
   Every other home (derivation, evaluation) is unproven or unbuilt. (§5.)
7. ∴ Build in this order: corpus + codebook + gold pilot → deterministic
   counters → one encoder extractor on the witness route → alignment with
   controls. Stop at any gate that fails. (§7.)

## 3. Hypotheses: the pattern as rates

Each hypothesis maps one paper move to one countable comparison. Thresholds,
effect floors, and α are **author decisions** (§8, D2) — none is stated in the
paper, whose falsifiers are docum

... [13207 characters truncated] ...

   taxonomy, thresholds, control definitions
gold/pilot-v0.1.tsv             double-annotated stratified pilot +
gold/pilot-v0.1.agreement.md    per-label κ/α, adjudication log, conflicts kept
scripts/enrich_stage2.py        deterministic counters (uv script, pinned
                                inline deps, no clock/network/randomness)
proposals/enrich-extraction-v0.1.tsv   one encoder extractor, witness route only
docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md    this file, versioned; results appended in
                                the §10 log, never edited into §§1–9
```

Plus one derivation-determinism spike report (§5, Route B): the extractor
run twice from empty on two architectures, byte comparison published.

**Go criteria — all three, or stop:** (a) annotators agree on the "promise"
unit at the pre-registered κ floor; (b) the shuffled placebo collapses to
neutral; (c) the peer filer's H1–H5 signature differs from Anthropic's. If
(a) fails, the construct is undefined and no model fixes it. If (b) or (c)
fails, the pipeline measures genre and §3 must be rewritten before any
further spend.

### v1 — only if the spike passes and the author promotes the needed law

Exhaustive extraction and alignment over the full corpus; H1–H5 with
confidence intervals; calibrated second-witness heads; external-outcome
sample check (§6.4); Risk–Governance Index v2 with the full S-1
risk-factor enumeration its v1 lacks — new **rows** in the existing
Status/verdict vocabulary, no new score column without a format bump; a
standalone companion results document with its own version and hash,
linked from the README document list, disputed under an attestation
protocol amended to name it as a target; new Zenodo version DOI. An
evaluation node kind or human-concurrence record ships only as a spec
amendment (§5), never as an implementation fait accompli.

## 8. Author decisions

- **D1 — Unit and codebook.** Sentence, clause, or claim? Promise vs
  aspiration vs condition vs risk-disclosure boundary; act time window;
  denominator. Nothing proceeds past the pilot without this.
- **D2 — Numeric falsifiers.** H2 outcome-share floor, threshold range, α,
  effect floors. Pre-register in `frameworks/promise-act-v0.1.md` before
  test data is seen.
- **D3 — Control corpus.** Which peer S-1(s), which comparator PBC, section
  matching, safe-harbour strata, placebo failure rate. EDGAR universe vs
  hand-picked peers is part of this decision.
- **D4 — Admissibility route.** Witness-only (held today) vs amending
  `descartes-spec.md` for derivation-route models and/or a sixth,
  evaluation, node kind — breaking the exact-five-kinds rule deliberately,
  with a named check. Human-concurrence and roster design ride with this.
- **D5 — Attach surface.** Standalone versioned companion (recommended;
  preserves paper v0, its hash, and future attestations) vs Index v2 rows
  vs paper appendix (new paper hash; attestations do not carry forward;
  re-signing required). The attestation protocol currently names one
  target; a multi-target registry is a protocol amendment.
- **D6 — S&P 500 sequencing.** Appendix E's corpus subsumes D3 at universe
  scale and adds the 0–5 mechanism test plus `Undisclosed` status. Decide
  whether the Anthropic spike is the pilot for that corpus (recommended:
  cyber-first, per Appendix E) or a separate single-company study. Running
  both with different codebooks would fork the construct.

## 9. What not to build

- A neural quote matcher. Byte-exact checking already solves it; fuzziness
  would weaken the one held guarantee.
- Embeddings or cosine scores as evidence, in any column, at any tier.
- BERTopic/UMAP clusters as signed output.
- Model-issued CONFIRMED/REFUTED verdicts. Verdicts are human attestations.
- Training labels generated by any LLM, above all the subject's.
- A single aggregate fidelity/alignment score
  ([`epistemics.md`](epistemics.md): loss per component per circle, never
  one number).
- An appendix bolted onto paper v0, or a silent `index.html` embed edit.
  Either moves the hash every attestation will name.
- Anything trained across tenant or subject boundaries. Designed
  prohibitions aside, it is also bad method here: the control must stay
  uncontaminated by the case.

### Silence the method must state

A filing-text pipeline hears only actors who produce citable text
([`strictness.md`](strictness.md), R1 testimony). Affected people —
authors, data-center neighbours, labelling workers, users — appear in this
corpus in Anthropic's voice or not at all; the paper's §8 says the same of
itself. The enrichment scores that silence as *unmeasured*, never as
absence of harm, and every results document carries this paragraph or its
successor.

---

*Results, when they exist, are appended below as dated records. §§1–9 above
are the pre-registration and do not change to fit them.*

## 10. Results log

*Empty. No corpus ingested, no annotation run, no model run as of v0.1
(2026-11-03).*

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb>=1.0", "blake3>=1.0"]
# ///
"""Item 1A risk-factor corpus extractor.

Reads the defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data SEC filing index on Hugging Face,
fetches 10-K primary documents from EDGAR, extracts Item 1A verbatim, and
stores bounded text with byte anchors.

Design constraints, per docs/descartes-spec.md:
  - P3 determinism: no clock, host, user or random id inside any hashed record.
    Time is a recorded input, passed in, never read here.
  - P1 doubt first: every extracted span is re-sliced from the stored text and
    re-hashed before it is emitted; a span that fails is dropped, not repaired.
  - Raw HTML is discarded at fetch time. Item 1A is ~1-3% of a filing; storing
    documents would be ~200 GB, storing anchored spans is ~2-4 GB.

    uv run scripts/rf_extract.py index                    # build local filing index
    uv run scripts/rf_extract.py fetch --limit 50         # smoke-test extraction
    uv run scripts/rf_extract.py fetch --year-min 2010    # full corpus
    uv run scripts/rf_extract.py verify                   # re-hash every stored span

No model, no scoring, no summary is produced here. This script only produces
verified verbatim text. Any downstream judgement is a separate, labelled step.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import html
import json
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
OUT = ROOT / ".rfcorpus"           # gitignored: bulk intermediate
DB = OUT / "rf.duckdb"
BLOBS = OUT / "blobs"
HF = "hf://datasets/defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data/data/US"
UA = "Anthropic-PBC risk-factor corpus research (governance@ethicalcapital.com)"
RATE_SECONDS = 0.12                # ~8 req/s, under EDGAR's 10/s ceiling

ITEM_1A_START = re.compile(
    r"item\s*1a\s*[\.\u2014\-:]*\s*risk\s+factors", re.IGNORECASE)
ITEM_1B_START = re.compile(
    r"item\s*1b\s*[\.\u2014\-:]*\s*unresolved\s+staff\s+comments", re.IGNORECASE)
ITEM_2_START = re.compile(
    r"item\s*2\s*[\.\u2014\-:]*\s*propert", re.IGNORECASE)
ITEM_1A_TOC = re.compile(
    r"item\s*1a[\.\u2014\-:]*\s*risk\s+factors\s*\.{2,}|"
    r"item\s*1a[\.\u2014\-:]*\s*risk\s+factors\s+\d{1,3}\s*$",
    re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE)

_pending_reason = ""


def canonical_hash(data: bytes) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(data).hexdigest()

-----
-----

A section whose closing heading cannot be found is **refused**, not stored. An
earlier version of this extractor allowed spans to run to end-of-document; DGX and
ALK were silently recorded at 362,210 and 279,612 characters, having swallowed
their exhibits and Item 15. Those spans were wrong, and the fix is to drop them.
A span with an unverified end boundary is not a long span — it is a failed one.

## 5. Integrity

Every span is hashed with BLAKE3 over its UTF-8 bytes, stored as
`blobs/<hash>.txt.gz`, and re-read and re-hashed before the record is written.
`uv run scripts/rf_extract.py verify` re-checks the whole store and fails on any
missing blob or hash mismatch. Current state of the smoke sample: 128 spans, 0 bad.

The hash is the claim's anchor: a downstream quote is verifiable only if it
re-slices to the stored digest. Determinism holds — no clock, host, user or random
id enters a record; the gzip mtime is pinned to 0.

## 6. Yield, and its honest limit

On the first 200 filings — which are the *oldest* in the window and the messiest —
165 extracted, 35 failed: 82.5%. Yield is expected to rise with filing year as
documents standardize, but that is a prediction, not a measurement, until the bulk
run reports.

**A failed extraction is not an absent risk factor.** The 35 refusals in that
sample are filings where the section exists but the boundary could not be
established. Any analysis of this corpus must report coverage — extracted ÷
attempted — alongside its findings. A risk that appears in 80% of filings is
interesting only relative to the 80% that extracted.

## 7. What this corpus does not answer

Item 1A is forward-looking by design: it asks what *could* harm the company. It
is structurally hostile to admitting a realized loss, and a search over it will
never find one directly.

"Has this risk produced a direct loss?" is answerable only by joining to other
filings for the same CIK — 8-K Item 2.06 (material impairments), 8-K Item 1.05
(cyber incidents), Item 7 MD&A, litigation disclosures. That join is a separate
extractor and is not built here. Any claim that a named risk caused a dollar loss
must cite the filing where the loss is booked, never an Item 1A sentence.

con = duckdb.connect()
for r in con.execute("""SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number, speaker, left(content, 160)
                        FROM 'sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet' WHERE symbol='MSFT' AND fiscal_year=2025 ORDER BY fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number LIMIT 12""").fetchall():
    print(r)
print(con.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT speaker), count(*) FILTER (WHERE speaker IS NULL OR speaker='') FROM 'sp500_ai_paragraphs.parquet'").fetchall())

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0", "blake3>=1.0"]
# ///
"""S&P 500 earnings-call AI corpus: deterministic, verbatim, byte-anchored.

Source: defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data on Hugging Face (ODC-BY 1.0), table
stock_earning_call_transcripts, pinned to one dataset commit. Universe: the
"S&P 500 component stocks" table of Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies,
pinned to one revision id. Both pins live in corpus/earnings-calls/MANIFEST.tsv.

Design constraints, per docs/descartes-spec.md and docs/risk-factor-corpus.md:
  - P3 determinism: no clock, host, user or random id in any output. Rows are
    sorted; parquet is written by a pinned DuckDB.
  - Verbatim only: every window is a [start, end) character slice of a stored
    paragraph, re-sliced and re-hashed by `verify`. Nothing is summarised.
  - No model, no scoring. Matching is a published regex; classification is a
    separate, labelled step (scripts/ec_classify.py).

    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py fetch         # download the pinned parquet, check BLAKE3
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py constituents  # pinned Wikipedia revision -> sp500-constituents.tsv
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py build         # calls.tsv, ai-paragraphs.parquet, ai-windows.parquet
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py verify        # re-slice and re-hash every window
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import re
import sys
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
BULK = ROOT / ".eccorpus"                      # gitignored: 2.3 GB source parquet
MANIFEST = CORPUS / "MANIFEST.tsv"
UA = "anthropic-pbc earnings-call corpus research (github.com/ethicalcapital/anthropic-pbc)"

# Term families. `AI` is case-sensitive (avoids "ai" inside words and "Ai" names);
# the phrases are case-insensitive. Python `re` and DuckDB RE2 accept both forms.
TERMS = {
    "ai":        r"\bAI\b|\bA\.I\.|\bGenAI\b|\bAGI\b",
    "ai_phrase": r"(?i:artificial intelligence|generative ai|generative model|gen ai\b)",
    "ml":        r"(?i:machine learning|deep learning|neural net)",
    "llm":       r"\bLLMs?\b|(?i:large language model)",
    "vendor":    r"(?i:chatgpt|openai|anthropic|\bclaude\b|\bgemini\b|copilot)",
    "agentic":   r"(?i:agentic|ai agents?\b)",
}
ANY = "(" + "|".join(f"(?:{p})" for p in TERMS.values()) + ")"
TERM_RE = {k: re.compile(v) for k, v in TERMS.items()}
ANY_RE = re.compile(ANY)
SENT_END = re.compile(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+")
MAX_WINDOW = 1500     # chars; longer sentence windows are clipped around the match
CLIP_PAD = 600


def b3(s: str) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(s.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def manifest() -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    with MANIFEST.open(newline="") as f:
        return {r["id"]: r for r in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")}


def source_path() -> Path:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    return BULK / m["path"]


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fetch
def cmd_fetch() -> int:
    m = manifest()["transcripts"]
    dst = BULK / m["path"]
    BULK.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    if not dst.exists():
        req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
        tmp = dst.with_suffix(".part")
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r, tmp.open("wb") as f:
            while chunk := r.read(1 << 22):
                f.write(chunk)
        tmp.rename(dst)
    h = blake3.blake3(max_threads=blake3.blake3.AUTO)
    with dst.open("rb") as f:
        while chunk := f.read(1 << 24):
            h.update(chunk)
    got, size = h.hexdigest(), dst.stat().st_size
    if str(size) != m["bytes"] or got != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: {dst.name} bytes={size} blake3={got}\n  manifest bytes={m['bytes']} blake3={m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    print(f"ok: {dst.name} {size} bytes blake3 {got}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- constituents
def cmd_constituents() -> int:
    m = manifest()["sp500"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(m["url"], headers={"User-Agent": UA})
    page = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30))["query"]["pages"][0]
    rev = page["revisions"][0]
    text = rev["slots"]["main"]["content"]
    if b3(text) != m["blake3"]:
        print(f"FAIL: revision {rev['revid']} wikitext blake3 {b3(text)} != manifest {m['blake3']}")
        return 1
    section = text.split('id="constituents"', 1)[1].split("|}", 1)[0]
    rows = []
    for line in section.split("\n|-")[1:]:
        t = re.search(r"\{\{(?:NyseSymbol|NasdaqSymbol|BZX link|Cboe ticker)\|([A-Za-z.]+)", line, re.I)
        cik = re.search(r"\|\|\s*(\d{10})\s*\|\|", line) or re.search(r"\b(\d{10})\b", line)
        if t:
            rows.append((t.group(1).upper().replace(".", "-"), cik.group(1) if cik else ""))
    rows = sorted(set(rows))
    out = CORPUS / "sp500-constituents.tsv"
    with out.open("w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n")
        w.writerow(["symbol", "cik"])
        w.writerows(rows)
    print(f"ok: {len(rows)} constituents from wikipedia revid {rev['revid']} -> {out.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- build
def windows_for(content: str) -> list[tuple[int, int, list[str]]]:
    """Merged sentence windows (match sentence +/- 1) as [start, end) offsets."""
    bounds, pos = [], 0
    for m in SENT_END.finditer(content):
        bounds.append((pos, m.start()))
        pos = m.end()
    bounds.append((pos, len(content)))
    hits = sorted({i for i, (s, e) in enumerate(bounds) if ANY_RE.search(content, s, e)})
    spans: list[list[int]] = []
    for i in hits:
        lo, hi = max(i - 1, 0), min(i + 1, len(bounds) - 1)
        if spans and lo <= spans[-1][1] + 1:
            spans[-1][1] = max(spans[-1][1], hi)
        else:
            spans.append([lo, hi])
    out = []
    for lo, hi in spans:
        s, e = bounds[lo][0], bounds[hi][1]
        if e - s > MAX_WINDOW:  # one run-on "sentence": clip around matches, snap to spaces
            pieces = []
            for m in ANY_RE.finditer(content, s, e):
                a, b = max(m.start() - CLIP_PAD, s), min(m.end() + CLIP_PAD, e)
                if pieces and a <= pieces[-1][1]:
                    pieces[-1][1] = b
                else:
                    pieces.append([a, b])
            for a, b in pieces:
                if a > s:
                    a = content.find(" ", a, b) + 1 or a
                if b < e:
                    b = content.rfind(" ", a, b) if content.rfind(" ", a, b) > a else b
                out.append((a, b))
        else:
            out.append((s, e))
    res = []
    for s, e in out:
        seg = content[s:e]
        fam = sorted(k for k, r in TERM_RE.items() if r.search(seg))
        if fam:
            res.append((s, e, fam))
    return res


def cmd_build() -> int:
    src = source_path()
    if not src.exists():
        sys.exit("source parquet missing: run `fetch` first")
    sp = CORPUS / "sp500-constituents.tsv"
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute("SET threads=8")
    con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE sp AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('{sp}', delim='\t', header=true, all_varchar=true)")
    con.execute(f"CREATE VIEW src AS SELECT * FROM '{src}'")

    # Speaker-role heuristic over the WHOLE dataset: sell-side analysts appear on many
    # issuers' calls; executives on one or two. Stored as a heuristic, never as fact.
    con.execute("""
      CREATE TABLE spk AS
      SELECT speaker, count(DISTINCT symbol) AS n_issuers
      FROM (SELECT symbol, unnest(transcripts).speaker AS speaker FROM src)
      WHERE speaker IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1""")

    # S&P calls, with a content hash to collapse share-class duplicates (GOOG/GOOGL).
    con.execute("""
      CREATE TABLE calls AS
      SELECT s.symbol, s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_quarter, s.report_date,
             len(s.transcripts) AS n_paragraphs,
             md5(string_agg(t.content, chr(10) ORDER BY t.paragraph_number)) AS call_md5
      FROM src s SEMI JOIN sp USING (symbol),
           LATERAL (SELECT unnest(s.transcripts, recursive := true)) t
      GROUP BY ALL""")
    con.execute("""
      CREATE TABLE canon AS
      SELECT *, first_value(symbol) OVER w AS canonical_symbol
      FROM calls WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY call_md5 ORDER BY symbol)""")

    rows = con.execute(f"""
      SELECT s.symbol, s.fiscal_year, s.fiscal_quarter, s.report_date,
             t.paragraph_number, t.speaker, t.content, coalesce(k.n_issuers, 0)
      FROM src s SEMI JOIN sp USING (symbol),
           LATERAL (SELECT unnest(s.transcripts, recursive := true)) t
      LEFT JOIN spk k ON k.speaker = t.speaker
      WHERE regexp_matches(t.content, '{ANY.replace("'", "''")}')
      """).fetchall()

    canon = {(r[0], r[1], r[2]): r[3] for r in
             con.execute("SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, canonical_symbol FROM canon").fetchall()}
    paras, wins = [], []
    for sym, fy, fq, rdate, pn, spkr, content, n_iss in rows:
        if canon[(sym, fy, fq)] != sym:
            continue  # duplicate share-class listing of an identical call
        ws = windows_for(content)
        if not ws:
            continue
        role = "operator" if (spkr or "").strip().lower() == "operator" else (
            "analyst_heuristic" if n_iss >= 3 else "issuer_heuristic")
        ph = b3(content)
        paras.append((sym, fy, fq, rdate, pn, spkr, role, n_iss, ph, content))
        for s, e, fam in ws:
            seg = content[s:e]
            wid = b3(f"{sym}|{fy}|{fq}|{pn}|{s}|{e}|{ph}")[:16]
            wins.append((wid, sym, fy, fq, rdate, pn, spkr, role, ph, s, e, b3(seg), ",".join(fam), seg))
    paras.sort(key=lambda r: (r[0], r[1], r[2], r[4]))
    wins.sort(key=lambda r: (r[1], r[2], r[3], r[5], r[9]))

    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE p (symbol VARCHAR, fiscal_year INT, fiscal_quarter INT, report_date VARCHAR,
                   paragraph_number INT, speaker VARCHAR, role VARCHAR, speaker_issuers INT,
                   paragraph_blake3 VARCHAR, content VARCHAR)""")
    con.executemany("INSERT INTO p VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", paras)
    con.execute("""CREATE TABLE w (window_id VARCHAR, symbol VARCHAR, fiscal_year INT, fiscal_quarter INT,
                   report_date VARCHAR, paragraph_number INT, speaker VARCHAR, role VARCHAR,
                   paragraph_blake3 VARCHAR, start_char INT, end_char INT, window_blake3 VARCHAR,
                   term_families VARCHAR, text VARCHAR)""")
    con.executemany("INSERT INTO w VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)", wins)
    if con.execute("SELECT count(*) - count(DISTINCT window_id) FROM w").fetchone()[0]:
        sys.exit("window_id collision")
    opts = "(FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 8192)"
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT * FROM p ORDER BY symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number) "
                f"TO '{CORPUS / 'ai-paragraphs.parquet'}' {opts}")
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT * FROM w ORDER BY symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number, start_char) "
                f"TO '{CORPUS / 'ai-windows.parquet'}' {opts}")

    # Denominators: every S&P call, AI or not.
    con.execute("""
      CREATE TABLE ai_by_call AS SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter,
             count(DISTINCT paragraph_number) AS n_ai_paragraphs, count(*) AS n_ai_windows
      FROM w GROUP BY ALL""")
    con.execute(f"""
      COPY (SELECT c.symbol, c.fiscal_year, c.fiscal_quarter, c.report_date, c.n_paragraphs,
                   CASE WHEN c.canonical_symbol <> c.symbol THEN c.canonical_symbol ELSE '' END AS duplicate_of,
                   coalesce(a.n_ai_paragraphs, 0) AS n_ai_paragraphs, coalesce(a.n_ai_windows, 0) AS n_ai_windows
            FROM canon c LEFT JOIN ai_by_call a USING (symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter)
            ORDER BY 1, 2, 3)
      TO '{CORPUS / 'calls.tsv'}' (HEADER, DELIMITER '\t')""")
    n = con.execute("SELECT count(*), sum((duplicate_of = '')::INT) FROM read_csv('" + str(CORPUS / 'calls.tsv') +
                    "', delim='\t', header=true)").fetchone()
    print(f"ok: {n[0]} S&P calls ({n[1]} unique), {len(paras)} AI paragraphs, {len(wins)} windows")
    return cmd_verify()


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- verify
def cmd_verify() -> int:
    con = duckdb.connect()
    paras = {(r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3]): (r[4], r[5]) for r in con.execute(
        f"SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number, paragraph_blake3, content "
        f"FROM '{CORPUS / 'ai-paragraphs.parquet'}'").fetchall()}
    bad = 0
    for k, (ph, content) in paras.items():
        if b3(content) != ph:
            bad += 1
            print(f"FAIL paragraph {k}")
    n = 0
    for wid, sym, fy, fq, pn, ph, s, e, wh, text in con.execute(
            f"SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, paragraph_number, paragraph_blake3, "
            f"start_char, end_char, window_blake3, text FROM '{CORPUS / 'ai-windows.parquet'}'").fetchall():
        n += 1
        p = paras.get((sym, fy, fq, pn))
        if p is None or p[0] != ph or p[1][s:e] != text or b3(text) != wh:
            bad += 1
            print(f"FAIL window {wid}")
    print(f"{'ok' if not bad else 'FAIL'}: {len(paras)} paragraphs, {n} windows re-sliced and re-hashed, {bad} bad")
    return 1 if bad else 0


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("cmd", choices=["fetch", "constituents", "build", "verify"])
    a = ap.parse_args()
    return {"fetch": cmd_fetch, "constituents": cmd_constituents, "build": cmd_build, "verify": cmd_verify}[a.cmd]()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "torch==2.9.1",
#   "transformers==4.57.3",
#   "sentencepiece==0.2.1",
#   "protobuf==6.33.1",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "blake3>=1.0",
# ]
# ///
"""Zero-shot NLI witness over the earnings-call AI windows.

Status: WITNESS ROUTE ONLY (docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md §5, §9). Every score is
a model's *proposal* about a verbatim window. No score is a verdict, a held
claim, or evidence that a risk materialised. No model is trained here; no
label is generated by an LLM.

Each window is scored against every hypothesis in the codebook by an NLI
cross-encoder: score = P(entailment) for (premise = window text, hypothesis).
Two independent encoder families are run so agreement can be reported:

    uv run scripts/ec_classify.py --model deberta      # DeBERTa-v3-large (MIT)
    uv run scripts/ec_classify.py --model modernbert   # ModernBERT-large (Apache-2.0)
    uv run scripts/ec_classify.py --model deberta --limit 200   # timing smoke test

Inputs and model weights are pinned (window file BLAKE3, codebook BLAKE3, HF
model revision). Output: proposals/earnings-calls/<codebook>/<model>.parquet,
long format (window_id, hypothesis_id, p_entail), plus run-<model>.json with
every pin and the software/device used. No clock enters either file.
Scores from different devices or library versions may differ in low-order
digits; derivation determinism across hardware is NOT claimed (spec §5, Route B).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import csv
import json
import platform
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb
import torch
import transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
WINDOWS = CORPUS / "ai-windows.parquet"
CODEBOOK = CORPUS / "codebook-v0.1.tsv"
OUT = ROOT / "proposals" / "earnings-calls" / "codebook-v0.1"
SHARDS = ROOT / ".eccorpus" / "shards"

MODELS = {
    "deberta": ("MoritzLaurer/deberta-v3-large-zeroshot-v2.0", "cf44676c28ba7312e5c5f8f8d2c22b3e0c9cdae2", "MIT"),
    "modernbert": ("MoritzLaurer/ModernBERT-large-zeroshot-v2.0", "a51e07b524299e309dd2b88d48b0cfa2bd9ec598", "Apache-2.0"),
}
MAX_LEN = 512
SHARD = 2048  # windows per checkpoint shard


def fhash(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def device() -> str:
    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        return "mps"
    return "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--model", choices=sorted(MODELS), required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=0, help="score only the first N windows (smoke test; writes nothing)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    name, rev, lic = MODELS[a.model]
    with CODEBOOK.open(newline="") as f:
        hyps = [(r["id"], r["hypothesis"]) for r in csv.DictReader(f, delimiter="\t")]
    wins = duckdb.connect().execute(
        f"SELECT window_id, text FROM '{WINDOWS}' ORDER BY length(text), window_id").fetchall()
    if a.limit:
        wins = wins[: a.limit]

    dev = device()
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name, revision=rev)
    model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(name, revision=rev, torch_dtype=torch.float32)
    model.eval().to(dev)
    label2id = {k.lower(): v for k, v in model.config.label2id.items()}
    ent = label2id.get("entailment")
    if ent is None:
        sys.exit(f"{name}: no 'entailment' label in {model.config.label2id}")

    SHARDS.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tag = f"{a.model}.{fhash(WINDOWS)[:12]}.{fhash(CODEBOOK)[:12]}"
    pairs = [(wid, text, hid, h) for wid, text in wins for hid, h in hyps]
    per_shard = SHARD * len(hyps)
    n_shards = (len(pairs) + per_shard - 1) // per_shard
    import time
    t0 = time.monotonic()  # progress display only; never written to any output
    for si in range(n_shards):
        shard_path = SHARDS / f"{tag}.{si:04d}.tsv"
        if shard_path.exists() and not a.limit:
            continue
        chunk = pairs[si * per_shard:(si + 1) * per_shard]
        rows = []
        with torch.inference_mode():
            for i in range(0, len(chunk), a.batch):
                b = chunk[i:i + a.batch]
                enc = tok([x[1] for x in b], [x[3] for x in b], truncation="only_first",
                          max_length=MAX_LEN, padding=True, return_tensors="pt").to(dev)
                probs = torch.softmax(model(**enc).logits.float(), dim=-1)[:, ent].cpu().tolist()
                rows.extend((x[0], x[2], f"{p:.6f}") for x, p in zip(b, probs))
        if a.limit:
            dt = time.monotonic() - t0
            print(f"smoke: {len(rows)} pairs in {dt:.1f}s = {len(rows)/dt:.1f} pairs/s on {dev}")
            full = len(duckdb.connect().execute(f"SELECT 1 FROM '{WINDOWS}'").fetchall()) * len(hyps)
            print(f"projected full run: {full} pairs ~ {full/(len(rows)/dt)/3600:.2f} h (short windows first; real run is slower)")
            return 0
        tmp = shard_path.with_suffix(".part")
        with tmp.open("w", newline="") as f:
            csv.writer(f, delimiter="\t", lineterminator="\n").writerows(rows)
        tmp.rename(shard_path)
        done = si + 1
        el = time.monotonic() - t0
        print(f"[{a.model}] shard {done}/{n_shards}  {el/60:.1f} min elapsed", flush=True)

    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con = duckdb.connect()
    con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE s AS SELECT * FROM read_csv('{SHARDS}/{tag}.*.tsv', delim='\t', header=false,
                    columns={{'window_id':'VARCHAR','hypothesis_id':'VARCHAR','p_entail':'DOUBLE'}})""")
    n = con.execute("SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT (window_id, hypothesis_id)) FROM s").fetchone()
    if n[0] != len(pairs) or n[1] != len(pairs):
        sys.exit(f"shard merge mismatch: {n} vs {len(pairs)} pairs")
    out = OUT / f"{a.model}.parquet"
    con.execute(f"""COPY (SELECT window_id, hypothesis_id, p_entail::FLOAT AS p_entail FROM s
                    ORDER BY window_id, hypothesis_id)
                    TO '{out}' (FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd, ROW_GROUP_SIZE 65536)""")
    run = {
        "status": "witness proposals; not held, not verdicts (docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md §5, §9)",
        "model": name, "model_revision": rev, "model_license": lic,
        "task": "zero-shot NLI; score = P(entailment | premise=window text, hypothesis)",
        "codebook": str(CODEBOOK.relative_to(ROOT)), "codebook_blake3": fhash(CODEBOOK),
        "windows": str(WINDOWS.relative_to(ROOT)), "windows_blake3": fhash(WINDOWS),
        "n_windows": len(wins), "n_hypotheses": len(hyps), "n_scores": len(pairs),
        "max_length": MAX_LEN, "truncation": "only_first", "dtype": "float32",
        "device": dev, "machine": platform.machine(), "python": platform.python_version(),
        "torch": torch.__version__, "transformers": transformers.__version__,
        "output": str(out.relative_to(ROOT)), "output_blake3": fhash(out),
    }
    (OUT / f"run-{a.model}.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print(f"ok: {len(pairs)} scores -> {out.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "bertopic==0.17.4",
#   "sentence-transformers==5.1.2",
#   "umap-learn==0.5.12",
#   "hdbscan==0.8.44",
#   "scikit-learn==1.7.2",
#   "numpy==2.3.5",
#   "pandas==2.3.3",
#   "torch==2.9.1",
#   "transformers==4.57.3",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "blake3>=1.0",
# ]
# ///
"""BERTopic map of the earnings-call AI windows. EXPLORATORY.

docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md §9 bars "BERTopic/UMAP clusters as signed output"
and "embeddings or cosine scores as evidence". This script respects that:
clusters are a reading aid for choosing what to hand-code next. They are
never cited as a finding, never a column in the Risk-Governance Index, and
never a verdict. Every topic lists window ids so any reading of it can be
checked against verbatim text.

    uv run scripts/ec_topics.py

Pins: embedding model revision, UMAP random_state, every library version.
UMAP with a fixed seed is reproducible on one machine and library set; it is
not claimed to be reproducible across hardware.
Outputs (proposals/earnings-calls/topics-v0.1/):
    topics.tsv        topic, size, top c-TF-IDF terms, three representative window ids
    assignments.parquet  window_id -> topic (-1 = unclustered)
    by-year.tsv       topic x fiscal_year window counts
    run.json          pins and parameters
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import platform
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import blake3
import duckdb
import numpy as np

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CORPUS = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls"
WINDOWS = CORPUS / "ai-windows.parquet"
OUT = ROOT / "proposals" / "earnings-calls" / "topics-v0.1"
CACHE = ROOT / ".eccorpus"

EMBED = ("sentence-transformers/all-mpnet-base-v2", "e8c3b32edf5434bc2275fc9bab85f82640a19130", "Apache-2.0")
SEED = 42
UMAP_KW = dict(n_neighbors=15, n_components=5, min_dist=0.0, metric="cosine", random_state=SEED)
HDB_KW = dict(min_cluster_size=60, min_samples=10, metric="euclidean", cluster_selection_method="eom",
              prediction_data=True)
VEC_KW = dict(stop_words="english", ngram_range=(1, 2), min_df=5)


def fhash(p: Path) -> str:
    return blake3.blake3(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def main() -> int:
    from bertopic import BERTopic
    from hdbscan import HDBSCAN
    from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
    from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import CountVectorizer
    from umap import UMAP

    con = duckdb.connect()
    rows = con.execute(f"SELECT window_id, fiscal_year, text FROM '{WINDOWS}' ORDER BY window_id").fetchall()
    ids = [r[0] for r in rows]
    years = [r[1] for r in rows]
    docs = [r[2] for r in rows]

    wh = fhash(WINDOWS)
    emb_path = CACHE / f"emb.mpnet.{wh[:12]}.npy"   # not committed: embeddings are not evidence
    if emb_path.exists():
        emb = np.load(emb_path)
    else:
        st = SentenceTransformer(EMBED[0], revision=EMBED[1], device="cpu")
        emb = st.encode(docs, batch_size=64, show_progress_bar=True, normalize_embeddings=True)
        np.save(emb_path, emb)

    model = BERTopic(
        umap_model=UMAP(**UMAP_KW),
        hdbscan_model=HDBSCAN(**HDB_KW),
        vectorizer_model=CountVectorizer(**VEC_KW),
        top_n_words=10,
        calculate_probabilities=False,
        verbose=True,
    )
    topics, _ = model.fit_transform(docs, embeddings=emb)

    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    con.execute("CREATE TABLE a (window_id VARCHAR, fiscal_year INT, topic INT)")
    con.executemany("INSERT INTO a VALUES (?,?,?)", list(zip(ids, years, [int(t) for t in topics])))
    con.execute(f"COPY (SELECT window_id, topic FROM a ORDER BY window_id) TO '{OUT / 'assignments.parquet'}' "
                f"(FORMAT parquet, COMPRESSION zstd)")
    con.execute(f"COPY (PIVOT (SELECT topic, fiscal_year FROM a) ON fiscal_year USING count(*) ORDER BY topic) "
                f"TO '{OUT / 'by-year.tsv'}' (HEADER, DELIMITER '\t')")

    # Representative windows: the 3 closest to each topic's embedding centroid (deterministic).
    t_arr = np.array(topics)
    lines = ["topic\tsize\tterms\trepresentative_window_ids"]
    for t in sorted(set(int(x) for x in topics)):
        idx = np.where(t_arr == t)[0]
        terms = ", ".join(w for w, _ in (model.get_topic(t) or []))
        c = emb[idx].mean(axis=0)
        order = idx[np.argsort(-(emb[idx] @ c), kind="stable")[:3]]
        lines.append(f"{t}\t{len(idx)}\t{terms}\t{','.join(ids[i] for i in order)}")
    (OUT / "topics.tsv").write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n")

    import bertopic, hdbscan, sentence_transformers, sklearn, umap
    run = {
        "status": "EXPLORATORY reading aid; not evidence, not signed (docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md §9)",
        "embedding_model": EMBED[0], "embedding_revision": EMBED[1], "embedding_license": EMBED[2],
        "embedding_device": "cpu", "normalize_embeddings": True,
        "umap": UMAP_KW, "hdbscan": HDB_KW, "vectorizer": {**VEC_KW, "ngram_range": list(VEC_KW["ngram_range"])},
        "windows": str(WINDOWS.relative_to(ROOT)), "windows_blake3": wh, "n_windows": len(ids),
        "n_topics": len(set(topics)) - (1 if -1 in topics else 0),
        "n_unclustered": int((t_arr == -1).sum()),
        "versions": {"bertopic": bertopic.__version__, "umap": umap.__version__, "hdbscan": getattr(hdbscan, "__version__", "0.8.44"),
                     "sentence_transformers": sentence_transformers.__version__, "sklearn": sklearn.__version__,
                     "numpy": np.__version__, "python": platform.python_version()},
        "machine": platform.machine(),
        "outputs": {p.name: fhash(p) for p in sorted(OUT.glob("*")) if p.name != "run.json"},
    }
    (OUT / "run.json").write_text(json.dumps(run, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print(f"ok: {run['n_topics']} topics, {run['n_unclustered']} unclustered of {len(ids)} windows -> {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
